summary.headline: FY26 revenue fell to about INR70.6 crore on customer-side delays, while H2 EBITDA margin rose to 11.77% and PAT reached INR3.25 crore.
summary.overview: Management attributed the year-on-year revenue decline to customer site delays rather than weak demand, with roughly INR31 crore of transformer orders and INR3 crore of another order deferred from March 2026 into FY27. FY26 total income was INR70.60 crore, EBITDA INR7.31 crore (10.39% margin) and PAT INR4.50 crore. H2 FY26 total income was INR42.59 crore, EBITDA INR5.01 crore (11.77%) and PAT INR3.25 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR120-180 crore, an EBITDA margin of 13-15% and a PAT margin of 9-11%, and said no dividend is expected for now.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue down about INR9 crore YoY per CFO (H1 FY26 vs H1 FY25 comparison as stated)
Management cited FY24 margin near 5% and FY25 near 11% (analyst framing)

financial_highlights.value: Transformers about 80% (about INR58 crore); PSS and CSS about INR8 crore; CSS and PSS about 10%

segments.name: Transformers
segments.commentary: About 80% of FY26 revenue, around INR58 crore. Inverter duty transformer of 17.60 MVA passed dynamic short-circuit test at CPRI; management says this is the highest rating in the industry for renewables.

segments.name: PSS and CSS (package and compact substations)
segments.commentary: About INR8 crore of FY26 revenue, roughly 10%. Management said package and compact substations together make up about 90% of the product mix.

segments.name: EV charging / NHEV
segments.commentary: Management said about INR31 crore of FY26 business came from the BESS-related segment. No BESS entry is planned, and the EV charging-station electrification role is a future opportunity, not yet booked.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR120-180 crore, with the deferred orders expected to be recognised in the current year.
Revenue growth guided at 60-80% for the next year, and 30-50% thereafter.
EBITDA margin target of 13-15% and PAT margin target of 9-11%, with about 10% as an average.
No dividend for now. Board may consider a dividend policy in 1-2 years, given working capital and capex needs.
Existing plant can handle about INR150 crore of business and up to INR200 crore if deliveries run smoothly.
Management expects to use about 90% of capacity in FY27 and says current capacity is at 75-80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Land identified for a new facility of about 2.50 lakh sq ft, to enter EHV transmission transformers and bring sheet-metal processing and powder coating in-house. The design is with the architect.
Installation on the ground is expected to start after 2-3 months, with at least 6 months needed before manufacturing starts there.
IPO funds partly used for working capital. The remaining plant and machinery funds are earmarked for new-plant machinery.
Current capacity is cited as over 1,200 MVA on the analyst's question. The management answer was unclear on the MVA figure, saying capacity of 120-180 (likely INR crore of business).
Robotic welding is being explored for fabrication. Management says automation can cover only 20-30% of the process in transformer manufacturing.
demand_pricing: Order book was about INR156 crore as of 25 May 2026.
Recent orders: INR9.70 crore of transformer and CSS orders. Vendor approvals from MVVNL, DHBVNL and UGVNL, and from Toyota and SMC-C Japan.
Bids of about INR125 crore in an MVVNL tender (total about INR356 crore) and about INR100 crore with Torrent Power. Torrent was the largest customer in FY25 at 35-40% of revenue.
Top six or seven customers make up about 45% of FY26 revenue, which management says reflects lower concentration.
Price variation (IEEMA clause) is included in tenders and in private orders above INR1 crore with delivery beyond 3 months. Some revision purchase orders have already been received.

Competition: multinationals (ABB, Siemens, Crompton) in high-end segments; Voltamp, Transformers & Rectifiers and Danish in western India. Management claims lower overheads and 100% in-house manufacturing as advantages.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue from operations decline in FY26 vs FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said revenue fell about INR9 crore because customer EPC projects were delayed. About INR31 crore of transformers (35 units, about 25 made, worth INR21-22 crore) and INR3 crore were deferred to FY27 after a Maharashtra government dispute and site delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend policy and when will capital be returned?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend is expected because the company is in an expansion phase with heavy working capital needs for the INR156 crore order book. The Board may consider a policy in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company entering BESS or energy storage?
qa_highlights.answer: Not currently. Management said BESS makers are existing clients, and entering that segment could cost those orders. Focus is on high-capacity, high-voltage transformers.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth and PAT guidance applies going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided FY27 revenue of INR120-180 crore, growth of 60-80% next year and 30-50% thereafter. EBITDA margin target is 13-15%, PAT margin 9-11%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company manage raw material price risk and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it keeps about 1-1.5 months of oil and accessories in stock, books copper and CRGO for about 1 month, and hedges about 15% for up to 3 months. Orders with delivery beyond 3 months carry IEEMA price variation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Russia MOU and the EV charging project worth?
qa_highlights.answer: The Russia MOU is with the Moscow industrial federation for technology transfer and a possible JV. No revenue is expected until the approval comes through. The NHEV project's CSS scope is about INR1,600 crore over 3-4 years on 450 stations, with an LOI issued and 10-15 stations expected by year-end.

risks_watch: Dependence on customer dispatch clearances and site readiness. About INR34 crore of deferred revenue is contingent on the Maharashtra dispute and EPC site progress.
Recognition of the INR31 crore and INR3 crore deferred orders in FY27 is needed to meet the guided INR120-180 crore revenue.
Margin target of 13-15% vs H2 FY26 level of 11.77% and FY26 level of 10.39%.
Working capital intensity of the expansion, with no dividend for 1-2 years.
Russia MOU and NHEV EV charging revenue timing is uncertain and depends on government and partner approvals.
Management did not fully reconcile the capacity figure (1,200 MVA raised by analyst vs 120-180 cited). Clarify in the next call.
Customer concentration: Torrent Power share dropped from 35-40% of FY25 revenue to a lower share in FY26. Customer details are to be provided in a separate note.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term demand and margins, but explanations for the FY26 revenue fall relied on customer-side delays and were not backed by hard dates. Answers on capacity, the MVA figure and the Russia and NHEV timelines were vague or conditional.
key_quotes: So the revenue was not recognized till March, but it is going to be recognized in the current financial year.
So currently, we are not planning into this because BESS is exactly different, and those BESS profiles are meant to be from our customer end.
But we manufacturing 100% in-house, so our cost of the manufacturing is less than others.
